findings.description: The woman leaves the bedroom through a doorway and enters a kitchen that is completely different from the opening kitchen: dark cherry cabinets with an over-the-range microwave and stainless gas range, versus the light-oak cabinets, brick-tile backsplash and countertop microwave seen at 00:00-00:01. In a single continuous take the geometry of the house does not hold together.

The distinctive blue-flower print that hung on the hallway wall (with a small orange picture beside it, 00:01.5-00:04.5) reappears on the bedroom wall next to a different doorway at 00:07.0-00:08.5, without its neighbouring small picture and alongside a new red/green abstract print. The same artwork appears to be in two places, or the room has morphed.

At 00:05-00:05.5 the bed has a nightstand with a lit lamp on its left and a window on the left wall. As the camera pans left at 00:06-00:06.25, the nightstand and lamp are gone from that side and the bed sits beside the window; a lamp then appears to the right of the bed below the painting, and a small side table with a photo appears that was not there before. The furniture rearranges as the camera moves.

In side and three-quarter views (00:00, 00:02.25-00:03.25, 00:05.25-00:06.25) the hair is a loose short layered bob. In rear views (00:00.75-00:01.25, 00:04-00:04.75, 00:07-00:09.75) it looks like a pinned, twisted low updo with curled tendrils. The hairstyle changes with camera angle.
A round loaf/dish sits on top of the countertop microwave at 00:00.0, is missing at 00:00.25 (only a small indistinct shape), then is back at 00:00.5-00:00.75.
A smeared, garbled rectangular panel hangs over the lower part of the colourful painting above the bed (00:04.5-00:05.5). It reads as a generation artifact, not a real object.
